hidden_data_integrity: AIME inputs are never mounted before scoring. Explore mounts student, teacher, train.parquet and MATH-500 only (declaration.py:21-43; comment at :32-34). Retrain mounts student, teacher, train.parquet and the patch (declaration.py:50-64). Only SCORE mounts data/aime and the verifier (declaration.py:111-117). The image copies only JustRL's grade.py and utils.py, no question data (environment/Dockerfile:91-96), and the build refuses any /opt/**/aime* (environment/check_image.py:132-135). /opt/harness/final_eval.py is readable (instruction.md:25 allows it) and exposes only source revisions and file hashes (final_eval.py:95-100), not questions or answers. Case pages report literal searches of all 60 final problems against each trajectory with zero hits.

Training data is decontaminated against the final set. train.parquet is DAPO-Math-17k (1,791,700 rows deduplicated to 16,395) with canonical, containment and shared 8-gram overlap against the pinned AIME24/25 removed, plus an 80-row holdout, leaving 15,285 rows (environment/assets.lock.yaml:115-142; tools/asset_builders/build_opd_zero_overlap.py:24,175). 8-gram filtering will not catch paraphrases, but no evidence of residual overlap was found.
The proxy does not leak. MATH-500 (JustRL test.parquet, assets.lock.yaml:168-178) comes from the MATH test set, which predates AIME 2024/2025, so the proxy and final cannot share items.

network_mode holds. task.toml:32 sets no-network; retrain and score run with --network=none (orchestrator/container.py:216-230). Explore egress is an allowlisting proxy, and case pages record blocked GitHub/NVIDIA/ChatGPT requests that returned no data.

Memorisation risk exists but does not differ between cells. The final is a public benchmark: 60 problems, answers widely published. AIME 2024 (Feb 2024) predates the fixed student DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B (Jan 2025) and the RL teacher JustRL-DeepSeek-1.5B; AIME 2025 postdates the student. The shipped components (AIME24 0.4958 vs AIME25 0.3583, instruction.md:38-39) fit easier or partly memorised 2024 items, though difficulty also differs. Every cell starts from the same student and teacher with the same data, so this shifts the absolute level, not the comparisons. UNCONFIRMED as a score driver.
scorer_issues: The proxy does not match the instruction. instruction.md:23 and task.toml:66 say both metrics use the 'rule grader with verifier fallback', but fast_eval grades with grade_rows, which is rule-only (fast_eval.py:30,223; grade.py:55-63). Only the final runs CompassVerifier on rule-rejected rows (final_eval.py:432-469). This affects proxy comparability only. Case pages for Sol none, Sol xhigh and Terra high flag the same defect.

LLM-judge fallback. CompassVerifier-3B judges every rule-rejected sample, about 1,100 of 1,920 per checkpoint (Terra max page: '1,108, 1,088, and 1,111 verifier fallbacks'). It is called with question='' (final_eval.py:412) on the full, untruncated response of up to 31,744 tokens, at temperature 0 (final_eval.py:406-424). The repo reports no agreement rate with ground truth or per-run count of verifier-accepted rows. The judge is from a different model family than the student, and no cell showed judge gaming. Logged as a caveat.

The final evaluator otherwise matches the instruction: 60 questions x 32 samples, T=0.7, top_p=0.9, 31,744-token cap, fixed sample seeds from Random(42) (final_eval.py:102-111,524), and a question-clustered SE (grade.py:89-111). Nothing can be reward-hacked through the checkpoint.
anchor_issues: The paper baseline 0.436 does not match the task's own shipped-recipe replay. instruction.md:36 and every case page give 820/1920 = 0.4271, with fixed start 0.2521 (instruction.md:35). Under 0.436, 5 of 25 scored cells beat the baseline; under the documented 0.4271, 14 do. All of these margins are inside noise.

An optimum of 1.0 (perfect AIME for a 1.5B model) is far above anything reachable. The best observed sigma is 0.121, and scored cells span sigma 0.090-0.121. OPD therefore adds about 0.1 per scored cell whatever the method. Cells without a valid patch get sigma=0, which is about 0.1 below any patch equivalent to the shipped recipe.
task_level.noise: The final has 60 questions; the question-clustered SE is about 0.052 per checkpoint (case pages: 0.0487-0.0539). The paired SE between two checkpoints is smaller, but the observed spread between near-identical weights is still about 0.005-0.016. Examples: Sonnet 5 high step 1650 vs 1651 gives 0.4109 vs 0.4266; Opus 5 medium 2200 vs 2201 gives 0.4323 vs 0.4276; Terra max 1800 vs 1808 gives 0.4349 vs 0.4219. 23 of the 25 scored cells lie in 0.418-0.449. The best cell is +0.022 over the documented shipped replay (0.4271) and +0.013 over the paper baseline, comparable to the one-step checkpoint jitter. No configuration can be distinguished from the shipped recipe or from each other, except Opus 5 max (0.392) and Kimi K3 max (0.405), which are lower but still within about 0.7 SE. The OPD ranking of configurations is noise.
task_level.checkpoint_selection: orchestrator/final_score.py:148 takes the max on the final metric. In 16 of 25 scored cells the reported checkpoint is not the last. Best minus last ranges from 0.001 to 0.020 in raw score (mean task sigma 0.0859 vs 0.0841 for the last checkpoint). Against the paper baseline 0.436, best-of-3 flips 4 cells from miss to beat (Opus 5 xhigh, Luna medium, Sol low, Terra medium). Each flip is a draw of evaluation noise on the test set and moves sigma by 0.012 or less.

task_level.summary: OPD's hidden-data boundary is sound: AIME is mounted only at scoring, training data is 8-gram-decontaminated, MATH-500 cannot overlap AIME 2024/25, and there is no network. The task's problem is resolution. With 60 public questions, the SE is about 0.052 and one-step checkpoint jitter is about 0.016. Every scored configuration (0.392-0.449) is statistically indistinguishable from the shipped recipe's 0.427, so the task ranks configurations by noise plus one binary: whether a valid nonempty patch was submitted (sigma ~0.1 vs 0). The paper's baseline (0.436) disagrees with the task's own replay (0.4271), which changes how many cells 'beat the baseline' from 5 to 14. The 1.0 optimum compresses OPD sigma into 0.09-0.12. Further caveats: the proxy lacks the verifier fallback the instruction promises, the CompassVerifier fallback is an unvalidated LLM judge that runs without the question, and best-of-3 selection on the test set flips 4 cells. These defects move sigma by about 0.02 or less per cell, so they are logged as MINOR and not counted.
